adjusted_prescription: Although the retrieved demonstrations show successful navigation near fires, they all involve paths through the central area and do not directly illustrate the left-edge corridor navigation needed. To fully support robust fire-avoidance and generalize the agent’s abilities, it is important to provide a complete example where the agent starts on the left edge, stays in the left-most column down to the bottom row, moves right along the bottom row towards the goal column, and finally ascends to reach the goal. This path should demonstrate the agent skillfully avoiding randomized fires placed away from the left edge, particularly those blocking other corridors. Such a demonstration will highlight long-horizon planning and corridor adherence strategies unique to the left-edge corridor, reinforcing safe navigation under dynamic fire conditions. Creating and including this left-edge corridor demo will improve the agent’s policy generalization and practical performance in diverse, challenging environments.
